thread:
sara (Support): Hey team — Customer `orion` is seeing intermittent 429s and higher-than-normal tail latency on their Dedicated pool since last night. They say calls succeed sometimes but often get 429s mid-request. Customer is on the new plan-migration we ran yesterday.

sara (Support): Pasted a snippet from their app logs: `Received 429 at /v1/generate (duration 230ms)`, then retry -> `200 OK` a few seconds later.

ashley (Account Manager): Looping in for context — Orion moved from legacy plan X to reserved-dedicated yesterday (billing migration). They reported cost delta and asked about limits, then started hitting errors.

devon (SRE): Thx. Can you drop the request-id + sample timestamps? Also which dedicated pool (region/pool-id)?

sara (Support): request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d, timestamps: 2025-11-03T01:12:34Z and 01:12:38Z. Pool: eu-west-2-dedicated-qa (pool-id: dp-775).

mike.ops: I pulled the backend rate headers for that request-id from the ingress proxy. Headers show: 

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1698972758
X-Quota-Units: 7200
X-Quota-Unit-Denom: HOUR
```

mike.ops: But our quota service is returning a quota key for that tenant with denom=MINUTE in the mapping table. Looks like a mismatch between plan-flag translation and quota-service during the migration.

joe-eng: Can you paste the rule we use to translate plan-tags -> quota units? I want to see if the denom conversion flipped.

devon (SRE): Here is the one-liner from the migration script that maps denom: `if plan.flag == 'new_rate' then denom='HOUR' else denom='MINUTE'`. The logic in the quota-service was originally expecting `per_minute` tokens; the migration inserted `per_hour` semantics into the billing table but didn't update the runtime mapping.

joe-eng: That explains the intermittent 429s. If quota-service thinks quota is per-minute (low) while headers advertise per-hour (high), the running limiter will hit remaining=0 quickly then briefly allow traffic when fallback checks succeed.

ashley (Account Manager): Customer wants a timeline and a mitigation ASAP. Can we offer a temporary increase to avoid user-facing errors?

devon (SRE): Short-term mitigation: update the quota-service override for tenant orion to match the intended denom (HOUR) and bump remaining to 95% of the new limit. That can be done via the admin console CLI: 

```
# temp fix
quota-admin set --tenant orion --pool dp-775 --units 7200 --denom HOUR --ttl 2h
```

mike.ops: Longer term fix: rollback the migration change that introduced inconsistent mapping OR update the quota-service to support both denom enums and a compatibility layer. I'll open a PR to normalise the mapping in the quota lookup and add unit conversion tests.

devon (SRE): Also schedule an autoscaler sanity check. Because the pool saw a sudden drop in allowed tokens, we saw queueing and then saw autoscaler try to spin up nodes which were ultimately not helpful due to per-tenant throttle — noisy neighbors made the autoscaler oscillate. We'll add a gating rule that ignores autoscale signals when >50% of recent rejections are 429s tied to per-tenant keys.

sara (Support): Repro steps we used from customer side: 
1) Send 5 concurrent requests with ~1000-token outputs at 1 req/sec to the dedicated endpoint.
2) Observe X-RateLimit-Remaining go to 0 within the first 60s.
3) Further requests return 429 until reset window or override.

sara (Support): Customer also sent a screenshot of dashboard showing "Quota units: 7200 HOUR" in billing UI but the Support debug output showed `denom=MINUTE` in the runtime mapping.

joe-eng: Can we get a dump of the quota-cache for dp-775 for that tenant? I want to confirm if cached entries are stale.

mike.ops: Dump attached (sanitized): 
```
{ tenant: "orion", pool: "dp-775", assigned_units: 7200, denom_cached: "MINUTE", cache_ts: 1698970000 }
```

mike.ops: Cache was populated during the migration window and not invalidated when the billing table updated. That's the leak.

devon (SRE): Immediate action items: 
- [devon] Run `quota-admin invalidate-cache --tenant orion --pool dp-775` and apply the temp fix (quota-admin set) 
- [mike.ops] PR to quota-service to add denom canonicalisation + conversion tests (assign priority P0) 
- [joe-eng] Add unit test that simulates plan-flag flip during migration and ensures cache invalidation hook runs 
- [sara] Communicate mitigation and ETA to Orion and confirm whether they want a retroactive credit for errors caused by misapplied limits.

ashley (Account Manager): I'll offer a 10% credit pending postmortem. Need exact window and error counts.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20251103-4012 — "orion dedicated 429s due to quota denom mismatch". Pager duty notified.

sara (Support): After applying the temporary fix, customer reported errors dropped to 0 within 90s and tail latency stabilized. They can confirm in 15 min.

devon (SRE): After fix we also observed autoscaler stabilise; no more spin-up loops. We'll keep the quota override for 2h and then deploy the conversion patch.

joe-eng: Adding a postmortem checklist: include migration-runbook update, verify migration tool outputs mapping summary, ensure cache invalidation hook exists, and add e2e for denom semantics.

ashley (Account Manager): Thanks team. I'll update Orion and schedule a follow-up call for 10:00 UTC.

sara (Support): Filing the support ticket with logs + steps and will link INC-20251103-4012.

mike.ops: FYI I'll also push a metric that tracks denom-mismatches (billing_table.denom != runtime.denom) so we catch regressions earlier.

sara (Support): Great. Marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if customer sees new 429s. :thumbsup:
